name: Justice Defenders
mission: JUSTICE DEFENDERS PROVIDES LEGAL EDUCATION, TRAINING, AND PRACTICE WITHIN DEFENSELESS COMMUNITIES. FOUNDED IN 2007, JUSTICE DEFENDERS WORK ACROSS 35+ PRISONS IN AFRICA WHERE INCARCERATED PEOPLE AND OFFICERS TRAIN AND PROVIDE LEGAL SERVICES FOR THEMSELVES AND OTHERS.
theoryOfChange: Justice Defenders has a published theory of change as part of their 'The Justice Defenders Way' document on their official website. This document outlines their 2025-2027 strategy, which includes expanding their work to '10 new prisons. Including planting a prison community in the United States.' The document explicitly states 'OUR THEORY OF CHANGE' under 'Our founding documents'. The 'The Justice Defenders Way' page describes their approach to bringing justice to those in need through legal education, training, and practice within prison communities, aiming to transform prisons into places of learning and service.

strengths_deep_dive: Justice Defenders provides legal education directly inside correctional facilities. According to organizational reporting, trained paralegals facilitated <cite id="4">15,338 court releases</cite> and <cite id="4">381 acquittals in 2024</cite> <cite id="4">[4]</cite>. This model provides critical legal representation in underserved systems, demonstrating documented direct outputs <cite id="3">[3]</cite>.
rich_narrative.summary:
Justice Defenders, founded in 2007, works to train incarcerated individuals and prison staff as paralegals and lawyers to defend the rights of defenceless communities in Africa <cite id="3">[3]</cite>. In FY2024, the charity recorded <cite id="2">total revenue of $1,331,729</cite>, down from FY2023 revenue of $1,868,837 <cite id="2">[2]</cite>. The organization maintains <cite id="1">an overall rating of 82.0/100 from Charity Navigator</cite> and earned a <cite id="10">Platinum Seal of Transparency from Candid</cite>.

While the model delivers clear impact by enabling <cite id="4">15,338 court releases in 2024</cite>, financial indicators present significant areas for consideration. In FY2024, the charity spent a program expense ratio of 58.5%, which falls below the standard 75% benchmark <cite id="1">[1]</cite>. Additionally, total spending in recent filings significantly exceeded annual revenue, drawing on financial reserves <cite id="2">[2]</cite>.
